Main.id: University of Chicago Laboratory Schools - Wikipedia#1
Main.sentence: The University of Chicago Laboratory Schools (also known as Lab, Lab Schools, or U-High , abbreviated UCLS ) is a ___E:private U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Private_school)___ , ___E:co-educational U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Co-educational)___ , ___E:day U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Day_school)___ ___E:pre-school U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_childhood_education)___ and ___E:K-12 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%E2%80%9312)___ school affiliated with the ___E:University of Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Chicago)___ in ___E:Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago)___ , ___E:Illinois U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois)___ .

Main.id: University of Chicago Laboratory Schools - Wikipedia#2
Main.sentence: More than half of its families are affiliated with the ___E:university U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University)___ .

Main.id: University of Chicago Laboratory Schools - Wikipedia#3
Main.sentence: The Laboratory Schools were founded by ___E:American educator U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Education_in_the_United_States)___ ___E:John Dewey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Dewey)___ in 1896 in the ___E:Hyde Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyde_Park,_Chicago)___ neighborhood of ___E:Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago)___ . ___E:Calvin Brainerd Cady U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calvin_Brainerd_Cady)___ was director of the music department under Dewey.

Main.id: University of Chicago Laboratory Schools - Wikipedia#4
Main.sentence: The school began as a ___E:progressive educational institution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Educational_progressivism)___ that goes from ___E:nursery school U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nursery_school)___ through 12th grade.

Main.id: University of Chicago Laboratory Schools - Wikipedia#5
Main.sentence: The school was an attempt to create a unified school system from the kindergarten to university.

Main.id: University of Chicago Laboratory Schools - Wikipedia#6
Main.sentence: Managed by the university's Department of Philosophy, Psychology, and Education, it served as a laboratory to test hypotheses and build on the knowledge about education because John Dewey, who became head of the department in 1894, wanted to test certain ideas of his.

Main.id: University of Chicago Laboratory Schools - Wikipedia#7
Main.sentence: In his book How We Think (1910), Dewey acknowledged the significant contributions made by his wife Alice Dewey to the school's early development.

Main.id: University of Chicago Laboratory Schools - Wikipedia#8
Main.sentence: The Laboratory Schools consists of two interrelated campuses.

Main.id: University of Chicago Laboratory Schools - Wikipedia#9
Main.sentence: The Historic Campus, located at 1362 East 59th Street, fills two full city blocks and is known for its ___E:Modern Gothic style U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Gothic_style)___ architecture.

Main.id: University of Chicago Laboratory Schools - Wikipedia#10
Main.sentence: It houses grades 3–12 (about 1,200 students) in five connected buildings: Blaine Hall (built in 1903), Belfield Towers (1904), Judd Hall (1931), the high school (built in 1960), the middle school (1993), and Gordon Parks Arts Hall (2015) which has 100 classrooms.

Main.id: University of Chicago Laboratory Schools - Wikipedia#11
Main.sentence: Two connected gymnasiums also sit on this campus, Sunny Gym (built in 1929) and Kovler Gymnasium (built in 2000) and students have access to both Scammon Garden and Jackman Field.

Main.id: University of Chicago Laboratory Schools - Wikipedia#12
Main.sentence: In September 2013, Lab opened Earl Shapiro Hall on its new Early Childhood Campus located at 5800 S. ___E:Stony Island Avenue U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stony_Island_Avenue)___ .

Main.id: University of Chicago Laboratory Schools - Wikipedia#13
Main.sentence: This new building, designed by Valerio Dewalt Train and FGM Architects, is home to approximately 625 children in nursery through second grade.

Main.id: University of Chicago Laboratory Schools - Wikipedia#14
Main.sentence: The building is named for Earl Shapiro, who graduated from Lab in 1956.

Main.id: University of Chicago Laboratory Schools - Wikipedia#15
Main.sentence: The school has approximately 2,203 students in total from Pre-Kindergarten – Grade 12.

Main.id: University of Chicago Laboratory Schools - Wikipedia#16
Main.sentence: Today, the school is divided into a Nursery School (Pre-K and Kindergarten), Primary School (grades 1 and 2), Lower School (grades 3 through 5), Middle School (grades 6 through 8), and High School (grades 9 through 12).

Main.id: University of Chicago Laboratory Schools - Wikipedia#17
Main.sentence: Many children begin in nursery school and continue through their high school graduation, and 75% of applications are for nursery school or 9th grade.

Main.id: University of Chicago Laboratory Schools - Wikipedia#18
Main.sentence: The student/teacher ratio is 8:1.

Main.id: University of Chicago Laboratory Schools - Wikipedia#19
Main.sentence: According to the 2021 Lab Student Wellness Survey, 48% of girls and 25% of boys, for a total of 37% of students, identify as part of the LGBTQ community.

Main.id: University of Chicago Laboratory Schools - Wikipedia#20
Main.sentence: In 2007 The Wall Street Journal ranked the high school fourth in the nation for its record of sending graduates to 8 elite colleges including its parent university, University of Chicago.

Main.id: University of Chicago Laboratory Schools - Wikipedia#21
Main.sentence: U-High offers more than 150 different classes.

Main.id: University of Chicago Laboratory Schools - Wikipedia#22
Main.sentence: All are college preparatory in nature and there are more than 30 Advanced Placement or Advanced Topic courses.

Main.id: University of Chicago Laboratory Schools - Wikipedia#23
Main.sentence: High school students may also qualify to take classes at the University of Chicago at no extra charge, and about 20 do so each year. The average composite ACT score is 31.5.  U-High uses a 4.0 unweighted GPA scale, does not rank students, and allows open course selection without academic tracking.

Main.id: University of Chicago Laboratory Schools - Wikipedia#24
Main.sentence: The school maintains four separate libraries  which collectively hold over 110,000 volumes.

Main.id: University of Chicago Laboratory Schools - Wikipedia#25
Main.sentence: High school students may choose from over 90 different clubs and activities.

Main.id: University of Chicago Laboratory Schools - Wikipedia#26
Main.sentence: The high school math, science, and ___E:Model UN U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Model_UN)___ teams are regular contenders for – and winners of – state titles.

Main.id: University of Chicago Laboratory Schools - Wikipedia#27
Main.sentence: The school's newspaper/website, The U-High Midway,  and the yearbook, U-Highlights, regularly win state and national awards, as does its arts magazine, Renaissance .

Main.id: University of Chicago Laboratory Schools - Wikipedia#28
Main.sentence: Other popular activities include theater, identity and affinity clubs, Student Council, policy debate, and Model UN. The Model UN team is consistently ranked among the top in the nation, and is world-renowned for its competitive excellence.

Main.id: University of Chicago Laboratory Schools - Wikipedia#29
Main.sentence: In 2011, it was ranked the #2 High School Model UN team in the United States.

Main.id: University of Chicago Laboratory Schools - Wikipedia#30
Main.sentence: The Debate Team has won numerous national circuit tournaments.

Main.id: University of Chicago Laboratory Schools - Wikipedia#31
Main.sentence: Organized by the Office of Alumni Relations Development, members of the student body at U-High are nominated by faculty to serve in the Maroon Key Society.

Main.id: University of Chicago Laboratory Schools - Wikipedia#32
Main.sentence: The Maroon Key Society serve as  ambassadors for the school, and they help provide tours to visiting alumni, potential students, and other guests to the school.

Main.id: University of Chicago Laboratory Schools - Wikipedia#33
Main.sentence: The high school's extracurricular activities occasionally make national and international news. For example, in 1990 ___E:then-Governor Thompson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_R._Thompson)___ declared a " ___E:Matthew Headrick U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthew_Headrick)___ Day"   and the ___E:US House U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives)___ made a proclamation  when then-student Headrick appeared on talk shows including ___E:Today U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Today_(U.S._TV_program))___   after winning the ___E:Regeneron Science Talent Search U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regeneron_Science_Talent_Search)___ .

Main.id: University of Chicago Laboratory Schools - Wikipedia#34
Main.sentence: In response to the award, the Chicago Tribune described the school as: "where being on the math team ... can actually enhance one's social status."

Main.id: University of Chicago Laboratory Schools - Wikipedia#35
Main.sentence: The Finance Club was founded in 2015 with more than $100,000 of donated funds to invest.

Main.id: University of Chicago Laboratory Schools - Wikipedia#36
Main.sentence: The 2019 boys soccer team won the IHSA 1A state championship.

Main.id: University of Chicago Laboratory Schools - Wikipedia#37
Main.sentence: The 2019 girls tennis team won the IHSA 1A state championship, becoming the first U-High girls team to win a state championship.

Main.id: University of Chicago Laboratory Schools - Wikipedia#38
Main.sentence: The 2021 girls tennis team was also 1A state champion,  and the team won the 1A state championship again in 2023.

Main.id: University of Chicago Laboratory Schools - Wikipedia#39
Main.sentence: The boys tennis team won the 1A state championship in 2018 and again in 2024,  making the 2023-24 school year the first time in school history that both girls and boys tennis teams won state championships in the same academic year.
